NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The proposed intervention is to install a sodium-ion-blocking interlayer between the cover glass and the encapsulant to prevent sodium migration into cell shunting paths. Standard practice uses a single encapsulant layer; this intervention adds a thin, commercially available barrier film with low sodium permeability as a separate layer. The closest existing practice is the use of barrier backsheet films in PV modules, but this applies the barrier to the front side, directly blocking the sodium source. The mechanism reduces sodium ion ingress by physically blocking the diffusion path from the soda-lime cover glass into the cell.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is Fick's first law of diffusion: J = -D * (dC/dx), where J is the flux of sodium ions, D is the diffusion coefficient, and dC/dx is the concentration gradient. The interlayer reduces J by introducing a high-resistance path (low D for sodium ions) between the glass and encapsulant. A commercial SiOx-coated PET film has a sodium ion transmission rate of <0.01 g·mm/m²/day (per supplier data), reducing the flux by >99% compared to bare glass (D ~10⁻¹² m²/s for sodium in glass), directly mitigating the driving mechanism of PID.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (all rows tagged per procurement rule)
- (a) Existing module lamination stack (glass/encapsulant/cell/backsheet)
- (b) Commercial SiOx-coated PET barrier film (e.g., standard food packaging grade, 125 μm thick, O₂ transmission rate <0.5 cc/m²/day)
- (c) Lamination process adjustment: Insert barrier film between cover glass and encapsulant during stack-up, maintaining existing lamination temperature/pressure profile

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Installation: Same as standard lamination (no new hardware) — same burden (tagged as a/b/c)
- Materials: Adds one standard catalog film (b), replaces no existing materials
- Process: Uses existing lamination equipment with one procedural change (c) — no new tooling
- Operational loss: Zero (no impact on module output or production rate)
- Burden class: Same as standard practice (film cost offset by reduced PID-related yield loss)

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: Accelerated PID test per IEC 62892, with 1000 V bias at 85°C/85% RH. Test group: modules with barrier film; control group: standard modules.
Instruments: IV curve tracer, thermal chamber, humidity chamber, high-voltage supply
Pass/fail criterion: Test group shows <0.5% annual power loss after 500 hours; control group shows >2% loss (typical PID rate).
Duration: 500 hours (equivalent to ~25 years at operating conditions)
Kill criterion: If test group shows >0.5% power loss, mechanism fails; if control group shows <2% loss, test invalid.
